pathwayLabel: Master: Reciprocity (Texas–Ohio Agreement) · Journeyman: No Reciprocity
examName: None for Master under reciprocity; Journeyman applicants take the Texas Journeyman exam (PSI)
steps: MASTER ELECTRICIANS: Ohio is on TDLR's Master Electrician reciprocity list (Alabama, Arkansas, Iowa, Louisiana, Nebraska, North Carolina and Ohio). TDLR announced the Texas–Ohio agreement on June 5, 2026; it covers "licensed master electricians and master electrical contractors."

Master requirements per TDLR's announcement: hold an Ohio state master electrician license in good standing for at least one year, obtained by passing Ohio's state-administered exam; each state's prerequisite requirements still apply, including journeyman licensure. TDLR's out-of-state page asks Ohio applicants for documentation showing a journeyman electrician license has been held for at least 1 year.
Master license fee: $45, per TDLR's out-of-state page. Under reciprocity, TDLR verifies that your original exam was passed and does not require a separate Texas exam.

JOURNEYMAN ELECTRICIANS: no reciprocity. Ohio is not on TDLR's Journeyman list (Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota and Wyoming), and TDLR's Ohio announcement states the agreement does not include journeyman electricians. Journeyman applicants follow Texas's standard route: 8,000 hours of supervised on-the-job training (7,000 to take the exam), the $30 application fee, and the $78 PSI exam ($108 total).
Await processing. TDLR does not publish a processing timeline on its out-of-state licensing page.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-01. The previous version wrongly said Ohio had no TDLR reciprocity; TDLR's announcement (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/news/2026/06/05/texas-expands-electrician-reciprocity-with-ohio-to-support-skilled-workforce-and-economic-growth/) and current out-of-state page (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/out-of-state.htm) both list Ohio for Master. Journeyman: officially not covered, per TDLR's own Journeyman list and the announcement's explicit statement, not merely unconfirmed. Headline fields (pathway, fee $45, no exam, 1 year) describe the Master path; the Journeyman path is in the steps. Journeyman figures from TDLR's Journeyman page (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/apply/individuals/journeyman-electrician.htm) and PSI's bulletin (https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/1682).
officialSourceName: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
indexingHold: Decided 2026-10-01: stays noindexed. Master (reciprocity) and Journeyman (none) have different answers, and the flat trade schema's headline fields (meta description, FAQ, score card) can show only one. Extending the schema for one page was declined; /electrician/texas separates both tiers from sourced data and is the canonical page for this content.
